As a graphic it passes the applicable craft checks (centred grid, modular scale ~26/44/90px, gray de-emphasis #707070, text contrast >4.5:1). tokens.notes: headline + wordmark; exactly Apple.com marketing near-black — deliberate Apple-page vernacular
burnt sienna; sole accent, used only for the ~8px strikethrough rule

patterns.key_values: marketing-hero composite (Apple-product-page grammar): centred single-axis stack, white full-bleed, one warm accent used as an editorial strike device. NOT an app pattern — brand evidence only.

signature_moves: Editorial strikethrough as show-don't-tell: a single burnt-sienna (#B44B23) rule through the words 'leave quietly' so the headline enacts its own claim — the whole visual-interest budget spent in one Von Restorff stroke (brand/marketing signature, not UI)
defects: Evidence gap (not an anti-pattern) — an uninstaller submitted with zero screenshots of the running app; the product UI is entirely unstudied
Icon reuses the macOS system-Trash silhouette wholesale — clever concept (uninstall = trash) but low brand distinctiveness; risks reading as the OS Trash can (soft brand flag, not a rubric defect)

aesthetic.direction: Apple product-page marketing (Swiss-adjacent restraint): near-white ground + Apple's #1D1D1F near-black SF Pro heavy display + a single warm burnt-sienna accent deployed as an editorial strike; mirror-centred, no shadow, no radius on type

psychology: Von Restorff effect — the lone burnt-sienna strike is the one different thing on an otherwise mono-accent white page, so it is what's remembered; accent budget spent exactly once
Processing fluency / picture-superiority — the strikethrough visually proves the claim ('apps don't ~~leave quietly~~'), so the message is grasped pre-read rather than parsed
First-impression thesis (Lindgaard 50ms) — icon + name + claim + one-line explanation answer 'what is this / who's it for / what does it do' within the first viewport
Hierarchy via de-emphasis — the explanatory copy recedes to #707070 gray so the black headline anchors attention (Refactoring-UI de-emphasis, not amplification)
